Inspectors conducted 2,590 inspections of vehicles transporting hazardous materials or dangerous goods (HM/DG). Those inspections resulted in 368 vehicle and 63 driver OOS violations.

Placarding was the top HM/DG out-of-service violation, with 40 violations accounting for 28.4% of all HM/DG OOS violations. Loading violations ranked second with 38, followed by shipping papers with 25.

What this means for the trucking industry

The 2026 Roadcheck results point fleets toward several areas that warrant continued attention, particularly brakes, tires, cargo securement, driver credentials, HOS, and ELD records.

The concentration of brake-related violations also reinforces the value of thorough preventive maintenance and pre-trip inspections. For fleet managers, the ELD findings show that compliance extends beyond having the required technology in the cab—accurate records and proper use remain critical.

The results also give fleets a practical checklist for preparing vehicles and drivers for roadside inspections, with mechanical condition, documentation, cargo securement, and electronic logging practices all affecting compliance.

On Sep. 6, General Motors notified dealers they will need to resolve an issue with a vacuum brake assist pump that makes it more difficult to engage the braking system and increases the risk for a crash. GM identified six models potentially afflicted with the defect between 2014 and 2018, totaling 3,456,111 vehicles in all. This includes two pickups—the Chevrolet Silverado (2014-2018) and GMC Sierra—and four SUVs, including the Cadillac Escalade (2015-2017), Chevrolet Suburban, Chevrolet Tahoe and GMC Yukon.

GM told CNN that the problem has resulted in 113 accidents  and 13 non-fatal injuries.

The problem appears to stem from excessive debris and sludge build-up on the vacuum pump filter screen as the engine oil lubricates it. This leads to a drop in vacuum and may necessitate more pressure applied to the brake pedal, create a “hard brake pedal,” and increase the time it takes to stop. Trucks and SUVs overdue for an oil change may be at a higher risk. Recalibrating the electronic brake control module to recognize lack of vacuum assist and activate hydraulic assist resolves the issue, GM says.

On the safety recall report, it’s noted that: “At all times, the brakes remain functional and exceed the requirements of S7.11 of Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standard (FMVSS) No. 135, ‘Light Vehicle Brake Systems.’”

The NHTSA opened the investigation last November and the Office of Defects Investigation received 111 hard brake reports from the various affected trucks and SUVs. Nine of the vehicles were involved in low-speed collisions, where it looks like the issue is more prevalent. The ABS system supplies supplemental hydraulic brake assist if vacuum drops, though at a lower level under low speeds.

GM is responsible for notifying owners, but you can also visit https://www.nhtsa.gov/recalls and enter your VIN to see if your vehicle needs to be brought in and repaired. The NHTSA Safety Issue ID is 19V645000. The dealership will reprogram Electronic Brake Control Module to fix the problem.

The Commercial Vehicle Safety Alliance (CVSA) revealed Brake Safety Week will take place August 23–29 to focus on commercial motor vehicle brake safety across North America. The alliance, which oversees coordinated roadside safety programs in Canada, Mexico, and the U.S., said trained inspectors will conduct routine inspections focused on brake systems and components.

Inspectors will pay particular attention to drums and rotors during this year’s brake-safety focus. Brake drum and rotor issues can affect braking efficiency and may result in debris dislodging from vehicles, potentially causing damage or injuries.

Vehicles found with brake-related out-of-service violations, or any other out-of-service violations, will be removed from service until corrected.

In addition to inspections, Brake Safety Week also emphasizes education and awareness. Inspectors and officials will engage with drivers, motor carriers, and mechanics to highlight the importance of proactive vehicle maintenance in reducing crashes and improving safety outcomes.

Motor carriers and drivers are encouraged to complete pre- and post-trip inspections to ensure all brake components are operating properly before vehicles are in service.

EPA’s proposed 2027 NOx rule revisions could affect engine costs and emissions compliance timelines.

Fleets face continued uncertainty as EPA reviews proposed changes to heavy-duty emissions requirements.

Equipment planning and maintenance remain critical as fleets prepare for potential regulatory changes.

The waiting game continues for the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) to issue its final decision on nitrogen oxide standards, widely known as the “NOx rule.” In July of this year, the agency unveiled its proposal to revise several provisions of its 2023 heavy-duty nitrogen oxide emissions rule but has yet to give the official green light to the rulemaking. With model year 2027 approaching, it’s important for fleets to understand where things stand.

To understand the status of the NOx rule today, we must briefly revisit 2023. EPA’s original heavy-duty emissions rule, which was finalized in January 2023, established more stringent NOx standards for model year 2027 and newer heavy-duty engines.

Under the rule, the allowable NOx emissions limit for heavy-duty engines drops from 0.20 grams per brake horsepower-hour (g/bhp-hr) to 0.035 g/bhp-hr—a reduction of over 80%. The goal was to significantly reduce nitrogen oxide emissions, which contribute to smog and other issues related to air quality.

The regulation also introduced testing based on low-load and idle cycles, which forced manufacturers to keep aftertreatment systems functioning while the engine was running relatively cold. Manufacturers were required to add large heating elements to their aftertreatment systems as a result of the testing modificaton.

The last additions were warranty and useful life extensions. EPA required emissions systems to maintain compliance for 50% longer (up to 650,000 miles) and required manufacturer warranties to be 450% longer (up to 450,000 miles).

This rulemaking raised concerns across the trucking industry about the cost of developing and manufacturing compliant engines as well as the potential impact on truck prices and maintenance. Some experts estimated a cost increase of as much as $15,000 for a new power unit in MY 2027.

Class 8 orders stall as EPA 2027 uncertainty lingers

EPA 2027 explained: What unresolved regulations and NCPs mean for future truck orders

Fast forward to July 2026, when EPA unveiled its new rulemaking to reduce the costliness of MY 2027 NOx standards. A key point: the proposal does not change the underlying NOx emissions limits or the tighter testing requirements.

Here’s a look at what the proposed amendments focus on:

Emissions warranty requirement: Maintain the current five-year/100,000-mile emissions warranty (the original rule, as stated above, increased coverage for heavy-duty engines to as much as 10 years or 450,000 miles).

Useful life requirements: Delay the implementation of extended useful life requirements from MY 2027 to MY 2030.

Diesel exhaust fluid (DEF) system requirements: Replace mandatory DEF-related speed and power derates with visible and/or audible dashboard warnings. Under the updated guidance, the final inducement speed increases from 5 mph to 25 mph, while the repair window massively widens from four hours to as much as 160 hours.

Nonconformance policies: The framework allows manufacturers to continue selling MY 2026-compliant engines for a small fee, called Nonconformance Penalties (NCPs). This gives manufacturers that are unable to meet the new standards on time an alternative to immediately achieving full compliance, provided they meet eligibility requirements.

The public comment period for the proposed rulemaking closed on August 29, and EPA has been reviewing the comments ever since. EPA has stated that it is working to finalize the rule as quickly as possible, but a final decision may not be issued until next year.

What fleets can do right now is focus on operational efficiency, maintenance excellence, and equipment planning that delivers value under any regulatory outcome. When the final rulemaking picture becomes clear, fleets that have maintained discipline will be in the strongest position to adapt.

With model year 2027 production weeks away, the trucking industry has consensus on how to handle the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency’s (EPA’s) looming heavy-duty emissions regulations—at least when it comes to rolling back the most expensive red tape.

Back in October, FleetOwner reviewed major manufacturers' regulatory filings and initial EPA 2027 compliance roadmaps to gauge what fleets should expect for next year's equipment plans. This month, we analyzed every major North American heavy-duty truck and engine maker’s third-quarter earnings report and investor call to see how their strategies—and pricing—are shifting just weeks before model year 2027 production begins.

While the industry is united on those cost-saving measures, 2027 powertrain strategies diverge sharply as manufacturers still face the EPA’s mandate to cut NOx emissions by roughly 83%—down to 35 milligrams per brake horsepower-hour starting January 1, 2027—alongside new low-load cycle standards.

Unless the EPA finalizes its July 2026 Notice of Proposed Rulemaking (Docket ID EPA-HQ-OAR-2026-0728), the 2023 Clean Trucks Plan takes full effect January 1, 2027. Here is how the proposed rulemaking would change the rules:

Tailpipe limits: Both frameworks cut NOx limits by roughly 85% to 0.035 g/hp-hr and halve particulate matter to 0.005 g/hp-hr.

Warranty relief: Cancels the 10-year/450,000-mile mandate, keeping the 5-year/100,000-mile standard to save $4,000 to $6,000+ per truck.

Useful life delay: Pushes extended full useful-life validation requirements back from 2027 to 2030.

DEF inducements: Eliminates mandatory speed limits and engine derates, shifting to audible chimes and visual warnings by 2029.

NCP safety valve: Authorizes per-engine fees—estimated at $6,000 to $7,000—to keep selling higher-emitting engines.

The division centers on the EPA’s proposed non-conformance penalties (NCPs). If finalized, NCPs would serve as a financial safety valve, letting manufacturers pay a per-engine fee to sell legacy 200-mg NOx equipment that falls short of the new, stringent standard. OEMs can also draw on banked emissions credits earned in recent years from selling equipment cleaner than current federal baselines.

Waiting on Washington to finalize NCP prices stalled the fall order season just as 2026 build slots sold out. Preliminary North American Class 8 net orders dropped in October to between 13,500 units (down 45% year over year, according to ACT Research , even as Classes 5–7 rose 14% to 18,000 units) and 15,600 units (down 36% year over year and nearly half the 10-year October average of 31,089, according to FTR Transportation Intelligence ).

“While spot rates remain supportive of equipment demand, the lack of clarity around EPA 2027 rules and associated costs has left OEMs and fleets unable to plan for next year,” Carter Vieth, research analyst at ACT Research, said. “It’s not a lack of desire for new equipment holding fleets back, but rather the inability to make informed investment decisions in the face of regulatory and economic uncertainty.”

With the 2026 pre-buy complete and plants near capacity through year-end, OEMs opened 2027 order boards with fluid pricing. FTR estimates that passing through NCPs could add $6,000 to $7,000 per engine for buyers, compared with an $8,000 to $12,000 premium for fully compliant 2027 engines. High fuel, insurance, and labor costs are also pressuring carrier margins and steering near-term capital toward trailers, noted Dan Moyer, FTR senior analyst for commercial vehicles.

“Weak October results suggest that some purchases may be deferred rather than canceled, potentially allowing orders to strengthen as emissions requirements, production schedules, and equipment pricing become clearer,” Moyer said.

Daimler Truck North America (DTNA), the lone OEM against the penalty option, wants customers to know that federal courts vacated NCPs during the 2012 emissions transition , ruling penalties are not meant to bail out manufacturers that choose not to adopt compliant technology.

That split forced North America’s heavy-duty truck and engine makers to choose between two paths for 2027: rely on NCPs and legacy engines to ease the transition, or commit exclusively to compliant hardware. Based on regulatory filings, company statements, and third-quarter executive earnings calls, here is where each manufacturer stands heading into 2027.

A year ago, purchasing a used car in the GCC often meant navigating limited information and a lack of transparency. In response, AutoData Middle East launched Vehicle Report – an AI-powered platform designed to place greater control in the hands of consumers. Over the past 12 months, more than 42,000 users have turned to the service to access verified data on ownership, accident history, valuation, and more. Daily usage has tripled between July 2024 and March 2025, with over 5,000 users now engaging each month. Of those, 84% reported no post-purchase issues, underscoring the platform’s role in reducing buyer risk and building confidence through accurate, accessible insight.

Empowering Informed, Efficient Car Buying

Vehicle Report stands out by turning fragmented automotive data into clear, actionable insight. Built around real consumer needs, the platform supports smarter, safer, and faster decision-making throughout the used car journey, before committing:

Save Money: Compare loan and insurance offers side by side, with market-aligned valuations to avoid overpaying.

Buy Smart: Access a car’s full history, including accidents and ownership lineage, maintenance data, pre-purchase inspection insights and service records, with a single Vehicle Identification Number (VIN) lookup.

Save Time: Instantly aggregating listings, while filtering and forecasting in real-time from multiple sales portals, streamlining the car-buying process.

Through this consolidated approach, the platform is shifting the regional automotive experience from reactive to data-driven, bridging the gap between information and confident decision-making for today’s car buyers.

As the UAE’s used car market continues to grow, residual value performance remains a crucial indicator of vehicle quality and long-term value. In Q2 2025, data from AutoData shows that family-friendly vehicles such as the Kia Carens LX continue to hold strong residual value (78% after 3 years), thanks to a balance of affordability, spacious design, and efficient ownership costs. Within the SUV category, the Toyota Land Cruiser GXR was recognised as the best-value model (81% after 3 years), combining robust specification levels with competitive market pricing and favourable depreciation profiles.

As Vehicle Report continues to gain momentum across the region, AutoData Middle East is expanding its suite of tools to support smarter decisions for both consumers and industry partners.

Among its upcoming innovations is an AI-powered pricing engine that delivers real-time car valuations using over 100 million data points – factoring in market trends, specs, and condition to reveal a vehicle’s true worth, whether buying, selling or trading in.

Also in development is Claim Hub , a tool for insurers to detect total loss vehicles, reduce fraud, and accelerate claims – enhancing accountability across the ecosystem and building long-term trust for buyers.

With a future-ready focus, AutoData is bridging data and trust to make car ownership safer, simpler, and smarter.

“Our mission has always been to bring clarity and confidence to the automotive ecosystem,” said Sebastian Fuchs, Managing Director of AutoData Middle East. “With advanced AI at its core, Vehicle Report delivers real-time, market-specific pricing and risk analysis – helping buyers save up to 25% on average. More than a history check, it’s a decision-making engine that unifies pricing, ownership, and insurance data to transform how used cars are bought and sold. As we grow, we’re focused on deeper integrations with insurers, banks, and marketplaces, and on launching tools like AutoMagic and Claim Hub to further streamline the process. We’re proud to be raising the bar for transparency and intelligence in automotive transactions.”

With AI-powered technology, trust, and transparency at its core, Vehicle Report is redefining how the UAE buys and sells used cars. Now entering its second year, it’s more than just a report – it’s a smart ecosystem built to empower better decisions, from valuation to insurance to ownership.

Learn more about Vehicle Report – AutoData Middle East’s AI-powered platform helping over 42,000 users make smarter car decisions: www.vehiclereport.me

Hyundai has revised its position statement to strengthen language regarding non-OEM parts.

The current statement, found on OEM1Stop, says: “Hyundai does not approve of the use of counterfeit, gray market, aftermarket, imitation, recycled, alternate, or other non-original equipment parts for collision repairs.”

The previous version stated: “Hyundai does not recommend the use of counterfeit, gray market, aftermarket, imitation, recycled, alternate, or other non-original equipment parts for collision repairs.”

Both statements list the above in all capital letters, bold, and underlined.

The statements say that Hyundai Genuine Parts help to ensure occupant protection and vehicle integrity.

“Use of counterfeit, gray market, aftermarket, imitation, recycled collision parts or any alternative or other non-original equipment parts for the repair of any collision-damaged vehicle may negatively affect vehicle crashworthiness and occupant safety during a collision and is not recommended by Hyundai.”

Hyundai told Repairer Driven News it updated the position statement to more clearly communicate its position on the use of non-OEM parts in collision repair.

“Because Hyundai cannot verify that non-OEM parts meet the same engineering, quality, and safety specifications as Hyundai Genuine Parts, we believe ‘does not approve’ more accurately reflects our position,” Hyundai said.

In the past year, General Motors has made multiple revisions to its position statements regarding non-OEM parts ; the most recent added the words “strictly prohibits” in red throughout the statements. Several of the automaker’s statements now specifically prohibit salvage, recycled, used, non-Genuine parts, and non-GM reconditioned parts in collision repair.

Ford and Lincoln also released an updated ADAS position statement in May that uses stronger language to say all standards in the document are mandated.

The pendulum is swinging, and major corporations with deep pockets are discussing the skilled workforce shortage, but that also means competition for a seat at the table will intensify, Jennifer Maher, TechForce Foundation CEO, told Repairer Driven News.

​“I worry that I don’t hear that same momentum in the collision industry,” Maher said.

​The U.S.Bureau of Labor has identified 47 different technician jobs using its standard occupational classification (SOC) system, Maher said. She said this includes everything from wind turbine techs to elevator technicians.

​“We’re all competing for the same person,” Maher said. “The person who is curious, likes to problem solve, takes it apart and puts it back together, gets a thrill out of making things work.”

​The collision industry competes with all of these different technician sectors, she said. The industry is also competing with all of the skilled trades, which include electricians, construction workers and plumbers.

​“You can’t just look at how to build collision techs in the collision program,” Maher said. “You have to cast your net really wide. We’re competing with all of those sectors.”

​Technicians are often overlooked in the conversation, she added.

​“I call them our hidden heroes because we all need technicians and we need to recognize and start talking about the importance of those service and maintenance technicians,” Maher said.

​As the pendulum swings, the conversation is heavily focused on construction jobs.

“I appreciate the need to bring back manufacturing and build more plants, build more housing, and build more data centers. That’s exciting and great, but in my world, I’m asking how do we keep what we have moving?”

​If technicians get lost in the conversation, then people will find themselves waiting on the tarmac because of a shortage of airplane technicians or waiting two months for their vehicle to be repaired because of a shortage of auto technicians, she said.

​“Techs are important and we need to be at the table,” Maher said. “That’s the bottom line, technicians need to be in the headlines and they need to be part of the excitement around the skilled trades.”

​The top 10 technician fields identified by the U.S. Bureau of Labor adds up to a workforce of 7 million people, she said.

​“Collectively they are a huge force but they are buried, hidden and not talked about,” Maher said.

​Even under the Bureau of Labor’s classification system, technicians are scattered throughout different industries including transportation, energy, industrial manufacturing and construction, she added.

​TechForce’s “Technician Supply, Demand & Opportunity Report.” found the U.S. economy is short roughly 140,000 skilled technicians a year, and the gap is widening, with 73,354 new collision repair entrant technicians needed by 2029 .

​It found that the collision repair sector sees the highest turnover of the 10 analyzed at 60.7%.

​Maher said TechForce Foundation continuously polls its 125,000 aspiring working techs to see which industries excite them.

​“I am worried about the collision industry because it does not resonate above the fold,” Maher said. “It is way down, way down on the list.”

​That is going to be a recruiting challenge for the collision industry, she adds.

​“It is a supply and demand economy,” Maher said. “When you look at wages, it’s not at the top. If it’s the same type of person and they start to learn their options, thanks to AI now, they can just ask. In the past, they didn’t know how to compare and they weren’t going to do that much research.”

​For every 10 collision techs needed, schools are only producing four, Maher states.

​“That leaves us more than 8,000 techs short every year, and what scares me most is that 6 in 10 leave their job every year,” Maher says. “Retention is just as big of an issue as recruitment.”

​Ford is one catalyst swinging the pendulum and auto and collision technicians have been a part of that conversation.

​CEO Jim Farley launched the ACCELERATE The Essential Economy event last year to start the conversation. It was held again last month .

​Through the event, the Alliance for America’s Skilled Trades was started and the State of America’s Skilled Trades: A National Report was funded.

​The Alliance has brought together major companies such as BlackRock, Google, Carhartt, NVIDIA, Microsoft and Milwaukee Tool to fund initiatives focused on the shortage.

​The State of America’s Skilled Trades report found the employment growth rate for automotive body and related repair to be 0.6% between 2019 and 2025.

​It also found that Auto body and other related repairers rank 118 out of 525 other occupations facing national shortage pressure.

​“Ford is looking at industrial manufacturing, who is repairing the conveyor belt, the robotic techs. And Ford dealerships are all over the country,” Maher said. “They know their product and their consumer and the challenges when it comes to hiring boots on the ground. Which is why they’re investing in solutions”

​Ford Motor Company and Ford Philanthropy make up TechForce’s largest donor at $4.5 million.

​“They support scholarships for people to become auto tech with no strings attached, “ Maher said. “It’s not like you have to go and work for Ford.”

​Ford has been at the forefront of having a strategy and a plan for the shortage, she said.

This includes Ford addressing the transportation issues that make a student dropout through a partnership with Lyft .

​Other OEMs are also working on the issue but everybody needs to invest to get students to the finish line, she added.

​“It is not just enough to change or enhance curriculum; people want faster, shorter ways to earn the credentials or training and get to work,” Maher said. “How do we accelerate that learning? This year’s MSO Symposium brought together “the Four Aces” — the CEOs of Boyd Group, Caliber, Classic Collision, and Crash Champions —in Las Vegas on Monday, who ultimately landed on a simple conclusion: the collision repair industry depends on the right people fitting into the right roles.

When moderator Dan Risley asked what they’re hearing from investors and other stakeholders about the industry today, Boyd Group CEO Brian Kaner responded that the industry isn’t “recession-proof, but it is recession-resilient.”

“There are plenty of opportunities for us to continue to grow our businesses,” he said. “It all comes down to making sure you have the right people in the right roles with the right capabilities. And if you have that and you know how to keep score and you can win with the insurance carriers and you can take care of their customers and really be the extension of what they’re looking for, this is a great business to be in, and it’s something that we can continue to all thrive in.”

However, in response to a different question Risley posed about the “temperature” of each MSO’s team leaders, Crash Champions CEO Matt Ebert and Kaner agreed it’s a tense, stressful time for them, and made some important points about estimators.

Ebert said being an estimator, or as Crash Champions calls them, a service advisor, “has to be one of the most miserable spots.”

“You’ve got technicians bitching at you, you’ve got management or ownership bitching at you, you’ve got insurance companies bitching at you,” he said. “Everything you do gets criticized. Everything you do gets reviewed and sent back, and you have to do it again. I wouldn’t last a week. I would quit that job and tell you to shove it up your a**. If you want to know the temperature of our people, that is the truth.”

Ebert added that general managers also face pressure to keep customers, employees, and insurance companies happy while trying to make money and handle the safety, legal, and logistical pieces of their jobs.

Kaner said the industry has a “compelling opportunity” to invest in people.

“You’ve got to make investments in estimators,” he said. “We all make investments in technicians. I think one of the bigger gaps we have as an industry right now is in estimators. There’s not enough of them. There’s not enough of them that understand the metrics. There’s not enough of them that are salespeople that can go help actually go sell a consumer-paid job. …it’s a tense time and anytime when you’re in an environment where volume is tight, it just ups the pressure of the organization.”

Brad Anderson, who joined the collision repair industry in June to take over as CEO of Classic Collision, said he believes all jobs in the industry are hard.

“We put a lot on them, and I think all of us as an industry and ecosystem have to consider that it all crashes down to the people at the shop,” he said. “The small changes we make up here get really big when there’s 20 changes happening to the individual, whether it’s a tech, a GM, a service advisor, so we’ve got to simplify the work.”

During the discussion, Ebert also noted that 40-50% of MSO employees don’t touch a car, which he said “presents huge administrative opportunity,” another point he and Kaner agreed on.

“We have 15,000 people in our organization, and half of them are technicians and the other half are the people that are just trying to get the car to the back and do all the administrative things that they need to do to get it there,” Kaner said.

The conversation also touched on declining repairable claims volume, with Risley asking what’s missing from that narrative.

Caliber CEO David Simmons said the overall picture on repairable claims is probably a little more positive than the data that’s often quoted, “even though it is bad.” The primary misleading point, he said, is repairable claims data being viewed as representative of the market.

“If you allow yourself to be defined by repairable claims volumes, you have 30 years of history of insurance premium inflation in one year followed by claims frequency 12 to 18 months later,” he said. “And the pattern recognition in that 30-year data set would show that when you get into mid- to low-single-digit insurance premium inflation, which we’ve been in for several quarters now, you have a lag to low- to mid-single-digit claims frequency increase. There’s reasons for optimism that the old pattern holds, kind of offset by a structural shift with consumers because of the shock factor of insurance premium inflation.”

However, outside of insurance claims, one point remains: people are still getting their cars repaired, but they’re paying out of pocket, he said.

“We don’t track the juxtaposition of [the] increase in the dollar value of direct customer pay against the decrease in repairable claims and the dollar value of that,” Simmons said. “If you look at that, the total market has come down, but it’s a lot different dynamic. Now we’re built to service the insurance carrier, so it requires some adaptation to get at this customer pay. But if you want, we have to adapt, but if one’s willing to adapt, that market segment is there, and it’s growing, it’s growing robustly.”

Simmons said he would love to see Mitchell and CCC “come together with a combined audited data set that is as close to accurate as possible on what’s really going on with claims, total losses, repairable claims, and segments of claims.”

Kaner said he thinks one thing people miss is that what’s happening in the industry isn’t all that different from what’s been happening.

“It’s like any ecosystem; something that happens can have a negative effect downstream, and this industry has the same thing,” he said.

In this case, “a very precipitous increase in premiums that then put consumers on heightened alert,” Kaner said, causing them to raise their deductibles, drop coverage, or not file a claim for fear of a large premium increase.

As the U.S. auto industry faces multiple disruptions, collision repairers are on the front lines of observing how consumers respond to changes in a sector critical to the nation’s gross domestic product (GDP), Kristen Dziczek, senior policy advisor at the Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago, said during The Industry Exchange at the Collision Industry Conference in Las Vegas.

“I think your shop is really where this broad economy meets people’s pocketbooks,” Dziczek said. “You’re seeing that decision made right on the front lines.”

Dziczek says those collision shop experiences will tell a story about the economy before data shows it.

“You’re seeing how trade increases the price of the part shipping,” Dziczek said. “You’re seeing how technology changes the things you have to do for calibration and the arguments you have to have about paying for those sorts of things. You’re seeing how finances change to higher deductibles; how the loss per mile is lower, but the loss per collision is higher.”

Part of Dziczek’s job is to have conversations with those throughout the auto industry, including collision repair businesses, about what they are seeing in the economy, she said.

“There’s a bunch of really smart people who are doing very complicated mathematical models of the economy, and we listen to all of that, and then they say, ‘And now, what’s really going on in the economy?’” she said.

Dziczek has been working at the Federal Reserve for about five years. Previously, she worked at General Motors, the UAW, in various auto industry roles for Congress, and at a nonprofit auto industry think tank.

“I think I have the coolest job in the auto industry,” she added.

Auto makes up about 5% of the U.S. GDP and employs more than 1 million people, Dziczek explained. She added that the industry touches all the “big moving parts,” like steel, aluminum, copper, microchips, oil, critical minerals, and magnets.

“We’ve got lenders, we’ve got insurers, we’ve got repair, we’ve got customers,” Dziczek said. “We’re [Federal Reserve] looking at consumer behavior, we’re looking at banking behavior, we’re looking at all sorts of things through the lens of the auto industry. It’s super duper important, and there are very few other segments of the economy that are 5% of the GDP.”

During the Industry Exchange, Aaron Schulenburg, executive director of the Society of Collision Repair Specialists (SCRS), asked Dziczek about the current and possible future pressures on the auto industry.

In 2026, gas prices, vehicle sales, tariffs, EVs, and technologies were some of the developments that the Federal Reserve paid attention to, she said.

“I’ll say this isn’t the highest gas prices have ever been, but it is the highest they’ve ever been this time of year,” Dziczek said as she ran through the list. “Sales have been remarkably resilient, coming in around $16 million this year. Consumers keep buying, so there’s been not really any kind of pullback with that. We’ve seen a few little blips from supply chain disruptions here and there, and then of course tariffs and how tariffs have played out.”

When discussing consumer spending, she said buyers seem to “be fine.” However, she added that new car buyers tend to make six-figure incomes. She added that there are some troubling signs with auto delinquencies, adding that they are at the highest level since 2010.

Dziczek said the EV reset has shifted focus to hybrids. Currently, about 16.7% of the vehicle market is hybrid, and some vehicles only have a hybrid configuration.

Electrified vehicles overall are about 24% of the market.

“That EV reset, however, burned about $100 billion in capital for the automakers,” Dziczek said. “A huge, huge turnaround, while the rest of the world continues on in electrification.”

Schulenburg asked if there are other vehicle technologies that the Federal Reserve is watching.

In response, Dziczek said two technologies that are most important to the collision repair industry: manufacturing changes to fewer parts and ADAS/automation.

Automakers are following Tesla’s lead on gigacasting to make vehicles less expensive, she said.

This year, Ford has been at the forefront of the conversation about gigacasting (or megacasting as Ford refers to it).

The automaker announced it would invest $5 billion to change how it makes electric vehicles to lower its EV prices. The target starting price for a mid-sized EV truck is $30,000 compared to the average EV cost of $56,000, according to CBS News .

The shift includes changing how the assembly line operates and a reduction in the total number of parts used in the vehicle. For example, a Ford press release says the wiring harness will be 4,000 feet shorter.

Dziczek said replacing many parts with fewer parts does make vehicles easier to manufacture but “maybe not easier to repair.”

It also could have implications for the companies that make the parts being reduced by the automakers.

ADAS and automation are changing the industry in other ways, she said. This includes federal regulatory actions and conversation.

In September, the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) announced an agreement with SAE to expedite the development of data-driven AV performance standards.

In March, NHTSA also announced plans to research ways to update its autonomous driving regulations .

The agency also mandated automatic emergency brakes as standard in vehicles by 2029 .

ADAS features do come with a cost, Dziczek said.

“Sure, my car can’t crash, but when the car that can crash runs into it, that bumper is very expensive,” she said.

For collision repairers, this means calibrations, she said.

Dziczek also said technology is changing how vehicles are manufactured.

Automakers are using AI from beginning to end, she said. This includes product design, supply chains, engineering, manufacturing quality, safety, and in the product itself, she added.

The majority of Volkswagen vehicles sold in the past decade have electronic parking brakes. However, most customers don’t even realize that the vehicle has an electronic parking brake, because the system engages and disengages the parking brake automatically on most vehicles. But, when the system fails and turns on the light or has a warning in the driver information center, then the customer will notice.

- Porsche TPMS: The First Carmaker To The Game

If you are doing a brake job on a vehicle with an electronic parking brake, you will need a scan tool with the proper software for the parking brake system to retract the calipers, adjust and perform diagnostics. There are no shortcuts on YouTube. You can find videos that involve removing the electric motor, jumping connectors and disassembling the parking brake mechanism. But, these methods are very risky and can damage the vehicle and kill productivity. Unapproved methods will set malfunction codes, and the worst-case scenario is that you could damage the unit.

The VW system that was installed on many of its platforms starting in 2004 is an example of a system that requires a scan tool to replace the rear brake pads.

The system has stepper motors on the back of the caliper that actuate the piston. The motor can be removed from the caliper, though the ignition should be switched off for at least 30 seconds before removing the connector.

The motor is sealed to the caliper with an o-ring around the spindle. The condition of this o-ring is critical for the life of the motor and should be lightly lubricated with brake fluid. If the o-ring fails, water and debris will be one step closer to the motor gears.

The spindle on the caliper can be rocked slightly with a torx bit so the motor seats in the spindle. Don’t force the motor assembly onto the caliper, because damage to the housing can occur.

On recent platforms, VW have outfitted the motors with a sensor that can measure brake pad wear and adjust the pads for the least amount of drag. During this adjustment on some vehicles, the pad thickness is calculated. The system counts the number of rotations of the motor with a hall effect sensor inside the unit.

Inspecting the caliper, hardware and motors may not give you a complete picture of what is happening with these systems. Having access to a scan tool can reduce diagnostic time.

The OEMs have built-in bi-directional protocols to retract the parking brake so the pads can be replaced. A dedicated brake tool or enhanced scan tool is able to command these protocols and interrogate the module for codes and faults.

The Electronic Parking Brake Module (EPBM) is the module on the CAN bus of most vehicles equipped with this system. Any missing data for vehicle speed, gear position or brake pedal input will cause a problem with the system.

Some systems use information from the electric parking brake to track shoe and pad wear. The system will count the number of turns the actuator makes or the position of the stepper motor to determine the thickness of the friction material.

If you do find yourself working on a vehicle whose electronic parking brake will not disengage, the first thing to do is look at the basics. Some systems require that the doors be shut and the brake pedal depressed. Some models may even require the seat belt to be buckled. Simple items like a defective brake pedal or door switch may hinder operation. Also, in some cases, the button may be defective. On some vehicles, the operation of the switch can be verified with a scan tool.

- Servicing Volkswagen Electronic Parking Brakes

The 2004-2013 Mazda 3 is based on the Ford global C1 platform, shared with the European Ford Focus and Volvo S40. Nothing is really groundbreaking about the mechanical brake system, but not paying attention to the details can end in a post-brake-job comeback.

A key service issue concerns the hydraulics and ABS system. The older the car, the greater the chance the brake fluid has not been serviced. Over time this can cause issues with the ABS hydraulic control unit.

For almost 10 years, Mazda used the same caliper, pad and rotor design. Pads should be replaced when there is 2mm or less of friction material. If the rotors are any thicker, they have enough material on them to last at least one turning on the lathe. The runout specification for these vehicles is .002” and disc thickness variation should be far below .0005”.

Mazda claims repeated panic braking may raise the temperature in some portions of the disc plate by approx. 1,000°C (l,832°F). This temperature is almost near impossible to achieve this side of a high-speed police chase.

The calipers mount to the brackets using caliper guide pins with Allen heads. The sleeves and boots should be disassembled, cleaned and lubricated every time the brakes are replaced. The torque for the guide pins is 21 ft./lbs. and the caliper bracket bolts should be tightened to 75 ft./lbs.

All Mazda3 models have rear disc brakes. The calipers mount to the brackets using caliper guide pins with Allen heads. The sleeves and boots should be disassembled, cleaned and lubricated every time the brakes are replaced. The torque for the guide pins is 21 ft./lbs. and the caliper bracket bolts should be tightened to 55 ft./lbs.

Mazda uses a hand brake that is incorporated into the rear caliper, and a couple of systems are employed to retract rear pistons. The later-model cars require the familiar method of turning the piston clockwise while applying pressure, where others will have a plug on the back side of the caliper that provides access for an Allen wrench to facilitate retracting the piston. Be careful as you retract the piston.

After the pads are replaced, pump the pedal and adjust the parking brake mechanism in the rear calipers. If the level has too much travel, perform the following steps:

Remove the service hole cover of the rear console.

Turn the adjusting nut and adjust the parking brake lever.

After adjustment, pull the parking brake lever one notch and verify that the parking brake warning light illuminates and the rear brakes do not drag.

The Mazda3 comes in two styles, ABS and ABS with Dynamic Stability Control (DSC). Both systems connect to other vehicle components via a high-speed serial data bus. The DSC system ties more components together (like a yaw/pitch sensor and steering position sensor) onto the bus.

If you are seeing communication-related DTCs, it is essential that you fully diagnose problems with the system before you start replacing sensors and modules. Some of these vehicles have been on the road for more than six years and the connections will be starting to corrode and fret.

One of the main facilitators of ABS/DCS problems are the connectors, especially under the hood where the control/modulator unit connects. Being able to measure values at the connectors and observe data on a scan tool is essential for diagnosing problems.

The biggest ABS issue with the three generations of Mazda 3 is power. With some higher mileage vehicles, the battery cables, wiring from the power distribution box or the ground connection (behind the driver’s side headlight at G02) can have enough resistance so the voltage drops below 8 volts. When this happens, the ABS module cuts control and the electronic brake distribution system is disabled.

If a modulator/control unit is replaced, the pressure sensors must be recalibrated with a scan tool that is able to communicate with the chassis/ABS module. If this is not performed, it can result in brake failure and lock up.

If you have DTCs C1141, C1142, C1143, C1144, C1233, C1234, C1235 or C1236 (ABS wheel-speed sensor/ABS sensor rotor), chances are something is wrong with the wheel bearings. Another cause for these codes could be an accumulation of metal debris on the sensor. The front bearings are press-in cartridge-style units. Rear wheel bearings are hub units. In the front, the tone ring, or encoder, is on the inner seal of the bearing and the sensor is mounted in the knuckle. The parameters for these codes to be set include abnormalities in the signal such as a weak signal or large differences in the value when compared to the other sensors.

If you have DTCs C1145, C1155, C1165 or C1175 (open sensor), it could be damaged wiring or a failed sensor that is the problem. If you have more than one, chances are there is a problem with the connection at the control unit or in the front or rear harnesses of the sensors.

These DTCs will usually clear themselves after repairs are made and the vehicle is driven above 6.2 mph when the self-diagnostic check is performed.

Some customers may report a slight clunk, bang or jolt from the front of the vehicle. This concern will most likely occur during the vehicle’s first forward movement and after the vehicle sits for a few hours and/or a cold soak. This is a normal operating noise of the ABS system.

If you encounter a customer complaint for this concern, explain that the noise comes from the ABS/TCS/DSC “Malfunction Detection Function” initial check. The initial check is a necessary function to ensure the normal operation of the ABS/TCS/DSC system. Regenerative braking allows electric vehicles to recover energy during deceleration. Instead of converting all vehicle momentum into heat at the brake rotors, the electric motor acts as a generator. This slows the vehicle while returning some energy to the battery.

- AutoZone’s Phil Daniele on ‘Putting Customers First’

- Niterra President and CEO Mike Schwab on ‘Delivering Trusted Solutions’

The process can significantly reduce the use of conventional friction brakes. However, reduced brake usage can also create maintenance challenges involving corrosion and component operation.

On conventional internal combustion engine (ICE) vehicles, brake pads regularly contact the rotors during braking. This friction helps remove light surface corrosion from the rotor faces.

EVs with aggressive regenerative braking may use their friction brakes less frequently. Exposure to moisture, road salt and humidity can then allow corrosion to develop on the rotor surfaces.

EV Regenerative Braking and Rotor Corrosion

Light surface rust is not necessarily a problem because normal brake applications can remove it. However, corrosion can progress when friction brakes are not used regularly.

Over time, heavier rust, pitting and scaling can develop on the rotors. Once the rotor surfaces deteriorate significantly, normal brake applications may not restore their condition.

Reduced friction brake usage can also extend brake pad life. However, brake components can develop problems unrelated to friction material wear.

Corrosion may form around brake pad hardware, caliper brackets, slide pins and other components. Pads can become restricted in their brackets, while caliper components may develop problems from limited movement.

As a result, brake components may require replacement because of corrosion or restricted movement rather than normal wear.

How Regenerative and Friction Braking Work Together

Electric vehicles still require conventional hydraulic friction brakes to maintain stopping performance.

Regenerative braking may become reduced or unavailable under certain operating conditions. These include a fully charged battery, very cold battery temperatures, vehicle stability control intervention or certain system faults.

EV braking systems blend regenerative braking with conventional hydraulic friction braking to provide the stopping performance drivers expect.

This makes conventional brake system condition an important consideration, even when regenerative braking reduces normal friction brake usage.

EV Brake Inspection and Maintenance Considerations

Technicians should account for reduced friction brake usage when inspecting electric vehicle braking systems.

Measuring brake pad thickness alone may not provide a complete picture of component condition.

EV regenerative braking improves efficiency by recovering energy and can substantially extend brake pad life. However, reduced friction brake usage can also increase the potential for corrosion and restricted component movement.

Brake condition assessments should account for both friction material wear and the effects of limited brake usage.

I was recently working on an ASE A5 test-prep article, and we reached the section on parking brakes. Most parking brakes act on the rear wheels, so the test is structured around that arrangement. But some vehicles have parking brakes on the front wheels. I knew that some older Saabs and Datsuns used front-wheel parking brakes. One modern example is the Buick Encore GX.

- Alignment Specs: 2021–Current Ford Mustang Mach-E

On these models, pulling the park-brake switch sends a signal to the Electronic Brake Control Module. The module supplies 12 volts to the apply-control circuits and ground to the release-control circuits, activating the left and right park-brake actuators and applying the brakes.

Pressing the switch sends a signal to the module to release the brakes. The module supplies 12 volts to the release-control circuits and ground to the apply-control circuits, activating the actuators and releasing the brakes. Depending on the vehicle, the switch may be a push-button style. Pressing it commands the parking brakes to apply or release based on their current position.

The parking brake will release automatically if the engine is running, the vehicle is shifted into gear, and the driver attempts to move off. Avoid rapid acceleration while the parking brake is applied to help preserve the parking-brake lining.

The Electronic Brake Control Module, also called the Brake System Control Module, controls the park-brake motor circuits and runs diagnostics to verify that they are operating properly.

To replace the brake pads, the park-brake caliper pistons must be fully retracted. There are two ways to put the parking brake into service mode. The preferred method is to use a scan tool with a service-mode function. If you do not have a compatible scan tool, use this procedure:

Turn the ignition on with the engine off.

Press the accelerator pedal halfway down.

Move the park-brake switch to the release position and hold it for 10 seconds. Release the switch.

Within five seconds, move the switch to the release position again.

The actuator bolts to the back of the caliper and is not included with a replacement caliper. If you remove the actuator, GM recommends replacing the caliper’s O-ring. Front-wheel parking brakes may be a novelty, but they make an interesting piece of trivia to test your technician friends on.

A driver rolls into the shop complaining that their tires are wearing out faster than expected. The vehicle drives reasonably well, and there are no obvious suspension noises. But a closer look at the tread tells a different story.

- Reading Brake Pad and Rotor Wear: A Diagnostic Guide

Uneven tire wear can reveal problems with alignment, suspension components, tire inflation and ride control. Learning how to recognize these patterns gives technicians a valuable diagnostic advantage.

The key is understanding what each wear pattern means and knowing which components to inspect next.

Start With Tire Pressure and Tread Depth

Before recommending an alignment or replacing suspension components, check the basics.

Inspect all four tires. Measure and record tread depth across the inner, center and outer portions of each tire. Compare the readings to identify differences in wear.

Next, check inflation pressure against the vehicle manufacturer’s specifications. Underinflation often increases wear along both shoulders, while sustained overinflation can increase center tread wear.

Don’t overlook the tire pressure monitoring system (TPMS). A warning light, damaged sensor or incorrect pressure setting may contribute to a problem that has gone unnoticed.

Also look for mismatched tires, damaged wheels and evidence of missed tire rotations.

These initial checks help determine whether the cause is tire maintenance, vehicle geometry or a mechanical problem.

Inner-Edge Wear: Check Camber, Toe and Ride Height

When the inside shoulder wears faster than the rest of the tread, alignment geometry should be one of the first areas to investigate.

Negative camber means the top of the wheel tilts inward relative to the vehicle. Excessive negative camber can place additional load on the inner shoulder.

Toe settings also matter. When wheels point too far inward or outward relative to the vehicle’s direction of travel, the tires scrub against the road instead of rolling cleanly.

Independent rear suspensions deserve particular attention. Worn bushings can change wheel geometry during acceleration, braking and cornering.

Shop tip: Measure ride height before performing an alignment. If the suspension is sitting below specification, adjusting alignment angles alone may not solve the problem.

Outer-Edge Wear: Inspect Alignment and Body Control

Excessive wear on the outside shoulder may indicate an alignment problem or excessive loading during cornering.

Positive camber, incorrect toe settings and worn suspension components can contribute to outer-edge wear.

Consider how the vehicle is driven. Crossovers and SUVs have relatively high centers of gravity, which can increase weight transfer during turns.

When springs, shocks or struts no longer control suspension movement effectively, the tire may experience additional loading and irregular wear.

Diagnostic reminder: Outer-edge wear does not automatically mean the shocks are bad. Verify alignment and mechanical condition before recommending replacement parts.

Feathering occurs when the tread blocks develop a sharp edge on one side and a smoother, rounded edge on the other.

You may not notice feathering immediately during a visual inspection. Carefully running your hand across the tread in opposite directions can help identify the pattern.

Feathering commonly indicates an incorrect toe setting.

However, toe can change when worn steering or suspension components move under load. That means the alignment readings may not tell the entire story.

Check for looseness in tie rods, control arm bushings and other steering components before making adjustments.

Remember that changing camber or caster can affect toe. That’s why toe is normally adjusted after other applicable alignment angles.

Cupping and Scalloping: Look Beyond Alignment

Cupping creates irregular high and low spots around the tire’s circumference. The pattern may resemble a series of shallow dips in the tread.

Shocks and struts help control wheel movement as the vehicle travels over bumps. If they lose damping ability, the tire may move excessively and develop irregular wear.

However, wheel imbalance can create similar symptoms.

Shop example: A driver complains of a humming noise that increases with road speed. The rear tires show scalloped wear, but there is no obvious wheel-bearing play.

Before replacing a bearing, inspect the tire surfaces, check wheel balance and evaluate suspension condition. Tire noise can sometimes resemble a failing wheel bearing.

A vehicle’s suspension geometry is designed around a specified operating height.

When springs weaken or suspension components wear, ride height can change. That affects camber, toe and the position of suspension control arms.

A small height difference may have a meaningful impact on tire wear.

Measure ride height using the manufacturer’s procedure and compare the results against specification. Don’t assume that springs are healthy simply because the vehicle appears level.

On vehicles with electronic air suspension, check for leaks and verify that ride-height sensors and calibration are operating correctly.

Don’t Forget Rear Alignment and Thrust Angle

Tire wear problems aren’t always limited to the front axle.

The thrust angle describes the direction the rear wheels point relative to the vehicle’s centerline. If the rear wheels are not aligned correctly, the driver may need to compensate with the steering wheel to keep the vehicle moving straight.

That condition can contribute to unusual tire wear and a steering wheel that appears off-center.

A four-wheel alignment can help identify these problems, particularly on vehicles with independent rear suspension.

When uneven tire wear enters the shop, use a consistent inspection process.

Verify the complaint. Ask when the wear started and whether the vehicle pulls, vibrates or makes noise.

Inspect the tires. Record tread depths, tire sizes, inflation pressures and visible wear patterns

Preparing for the next generation of vehicles takes money and so does keeping up with the ones already in the shop. When you consider investments for 2027, both of those aspects deserve attention. The challenge is deciding how much to commit to each as repair needs develop at different speeds.

- AI Can Do the Math. Humans Still Make the Magic.

- AI & the Aftermarket: NTN Bearing Corporation of America’s Charles Harris

- Are We Asking the Wrong Questions About AI?

The headlines that flooded AftermarketNews website in the past month offer a useful view of that balancing act. Suppliers are developing products for electric drive units while expanding conventional transmission coverage. They are advancing familiar battery technology and redesigning components around problems that emerge after years of use. The opportunities span vehicles of different ages and technologies, all competing for a place in the business plan.

The latest powertrain forecast from the Auto Care Association and MEMA Aftermarket Suppliers helps explain why such planning requires patience. Developed with Strategy&, PwC’s strategy division, the report projects hybrids will account for 32% of U.S. new-vehicle sales in 2035, up from 17% in 2026. It also expects the number of hybrid models to triple between 2025 and 2035.

“Hybrids are becoming a bigger part of the picture, and suppliers need to plan for that reality,” said Philip Atkins, director of strategic research and planning at MEMA Aftermarket Suppliers. “The mix of vehicles on the road will keep changing, and understanding where that demand is headed will help companies make better decisions about products and investment.”

Those are new-vehicle sales projections. Their implications for independent repair develop over time, as vehicles age and their service requirements become clearer. Some of that change is happening within categories the aftermarket already knows well.

Clarios’ expansion of its hAGM battery technology, for example, addresses growing demands on low-voltage electrical systems across powertrain types. More electronics, connectivity and energy-management functions place additional demands on the 12-volt battery, including when the vehicle is parked. The company is applying the technology to future original-equipment programs and, through its OPTIMA REDTOP with hAGM+ technology, the premium replacement market.

“The technology trends shaping future vehicles will also shape the replacement market,” said Marc Andraca, president of U.S. and Canada region at Clarios.

So even a well-established replacement category can require continued development as the systems around it change. Familiarity with the product does not settle the question of what customers will need from its next generation.

Schaeffler’s recent portfolio announcements show how several investment horizons can sit alongside one another. The company is expanding electronics capabilities through its integration of Vitesco Technologies and adding conventional transmission coverage, including an 8L90 torque converter. Its E-Axle RepSystem 2 in1 bearing repair kit enables targeted repairs within electric drive units as an alternative to replacing larger assemblies.

Each addresses a particular repair need, but taken together, they illustrate the breadth of development work that a more varied vehicle population can require. The investment extends into what information and technical support do customers need to use those products?

Dorman’s new aluminum oil filter housing brings the discussion back to an existing application. Designed for select Genesis, Hyundai and Kia vehicles, it addresses an original equipment plastic housing that the company said can degrade, warp or crack after prolonged exposure to heat and chemicals. Dorman’s replacement uses high-pressure die-cast aluminum to address that weakness.

For leaders weighing next year’s commitments, these stories suggest that the timing of investment deserves as much scrutiny as its direction. Vehicle populations, emerging failure points and customer experience can help test whether an opportunity is becoming ready for the business to serve.

The vehicles that will shape the aftermarket’s next decade are entering service alongside those that still have years of repairs ahead. Preparing for that future means staying close enough to customers to recognize what is arriving in their bays, then putting the right resources behind it.

The Schaeffler division is making two Vitesco repair solutions available to the automotive aftermarket: a Voltage Stabilization System (VSS) for micro hybrid vehicles from Toyota and Peugeot S.A. (PSA), and a 48V DC/DC converter for Ford mild hybrid vehicles.

- Preventing EV Lithium-ion Battery Fires

- Charging and Replacing Batteries with Advanced Power Management Systems

The VSS is available immediately. According to Schaeffler, it prevents voltage drops that can occur during automatic start-stop operation in micro-hybrid vehicles. The system consists of an Energy Storage System (ESS) with high-performance capacitors and a Power Electronics Unit (PEU).

Schaeffler notes that during the engine start process, the capacitors release energy stored while driving within a very short time, compensating for the high-power demand. Starting the engine via a starter-generator requires a comparatively high amount of energy.

If this energy is drawn solely from the conventional 12-volt electrical system, the voltage can briefly drop by several volts, causing visible flickering of the vehicle’s lighting and electronic displays. Schaeffler said that by stabilizing the voltage supply, the capacitors ensure smooth engine restarting and contribute to longer battery life, improved driving comfort and compliance with current emissions standards.

The Schaeffler Vitesco 48V DC/DC converter, available in May, is used in mild-hybrid vehicles equipped with a 48V starter generator and an additional battery to enable more efficient power delivery and boost performance during acceleration, the company says. The converter links the vehicle’s 48-volt electrical system with the 12-volt onboard electronics.

The converter is a component of energy management in mild-hybrid vehicles and for achieving type-approval compliant CO2 emissions. Its bidirectional design allows 12-volt components to be supplied from the 48-volt network while charging the starter battery. Conversely, in the event of a temporary failure, the 48-volt system can also draw energy from the 12-volt network, the company notes.

Regenerative braking allows electric vehicles to recover energy during deceleration. Instead of converting all vehicle momentum into heat at the brake rotors, the electric motor acts as a generator. This slows the vehicle while returning some energy to the battery.

- AutoZone’s Phil Daniele on ‘Putting Customers First’

- Dipstick Replacement Sensors: How They Work

- Don’t Forget Lubrication During an Oil Change

The process can significantly reduce the use of conventional friction brakes. However, reduced brake usage can also create maintenance challenges involving corrosion and component operation.

On conventional internal combustion engine (ICE) vehicles, brake pads regularly contact the rotors during braking. This friction helps remove light surface corrosion from the rotor faces.

EVs with aggressive regenerative braking may use their friction brakes less frequently. Exposure to moisture, road salt and humidity can then allow corrosion to develop on the rotor surfaces.

EV Regenerative Braking and Rotor Corrosion

Light surface rust is not necessarily a problem because normal brake applications can remove it. However, corrosion can progress when friction brakes are not used regularly.

Over time, heavier rust, pitting and scaling can develop on the rotors. Once the rotor surfaces deteriorate significantly, normal brake applications may not restore their condition.

Reduced friction brake usage can also extend brake pad life. However, brake components can develop problems unrelated to friction material wear.

Corrosion may form around brake pad hardware, caliper brackets, slide pins and other components. Pads can become restricted in their brackets, while caliper components may develop problems from limited movement.

As a result, brake components may require replacement because of corrosion or restricted movement rather than normal wear.

How Regenerative and Friction Braking Work Together

Electric vehicles still require conventional hydraulic friction brakes to maintain stopping performance.

Regenerative braking may become reduced or unavailable under certain operating conditions. These include a fully charged battery, very cold battery temperatures, vehicle stability control intervention or certain system faults.

EV braking systems blend regenerative braking with conventional hydraulic friction braking to provide the stopping performance drivers expect.

This makes conventional brake system condition an important consideration, even when regenerative braking reduces normal friction brake usage.

EV Brake Inspection and Maintenance Considerations

Technicians should account for reduced friction brake usage when inspecting electric vehicle braking systems.

Measuring brake pad thickness alone may not provide a complete picture of component condition.

EV regenerative braking improves efficiency by recovering energy and can substantially extend brake pad life. However, reduced friction brake usage can also increase the potential for corrosion and restricted component movement.

Brake condition assessments should account for both friction material wear and the effects of limited brake usage.

株式会社アドヴィックス（本社：愛知県刈谷市、社長：秋山晃、以下、アドヴィックス）は、ドイツ自動車工業会（VDA）が設計した情報セキュリティの基準であるTISAX（Trusted Information Security Assessment Exchange）認証を取得しました。

近年、自動車業界においては重要な情報を他社と共有し製品を共同開発する動きが活発になっています。共有する情報の中には機密性の高い内容が含まれているため、サプライチェーン全体でセキュリティレベルの把握と高度な情報セキュリティ対策の強化が喫緊で求められています。

TISAXは、自動車業界のサプライチェーン全体で、情報セキュリティ水準を共通の基準で評価・共有するための業界標準の認証（評価）制度です。TISAX認証を取得することで、情報セキュリティレベルを客観的に証明できるため、顧客や取引先からの信頼性が向上します。また、共有プラットフォーム上で評価結果を確認することができるので、個社毎に審査や回答を行う必要がなくなり、取引開始までのプロセスを大幅に効率化できます。今回の本社拠点での認証取得を皮切りに、欧州をはじめとした各地域の開発拠点での取得を目指します。

アドヴィックスは、情報セキュリティ体制の継続的な強化に取り組み、お客様と社会から信頼される企業であり続けてまいります。

BETHESDA, Md . — January 14, 2026 — The Auto Care Association today thanked the United States House Committee on Energy and Commerce’s Subcommittee on Commerce, Manufacturing, and Trade (CMT) for holding a timely and important hearing to examine legislative options to strengthen motor vehicle safety, ensure consumer choice and affordability, and cement U.S. automotive leadership.

The association commended Chairman Bilirakis, R-Fla.-12, Ranking Member Schakowsky, D-Ill.-9, and members of the Subcommittee for their leadership and thoughtful consideration of bipartisan solutions that recognize the rapidly evolving nature of vehicle technology and its impact on safety, repair, and consumer costs.

In testimony provided to the subcommittee, Auto Care Association President and CEO Bill Hanvey emphasized that safe, affordable, and accessible vehicle repair is essential to highway safety and consumer protection, particularly as vehicles become increasingly software-driven and data-dependent.

“Today’s vehicles are computers on wheels,” Hanvey said, noting that manufacturers are increasingly restricting access to critical repair and maintenance data. “When vehicle owners and independent repairers are locked out of that data, repairs are delayed, costs increase, and safety can be compromised.”

Hanvey underscored the importance of including the Right to Equitable and Professional Auto Industry Repair (REPAIR) Act (H.R. 1566) in the safety title of the upcoming Surface Transportation Reauthorization Act. He highlighted that the bipartisan legislation, supported by 42 cosponsors and more than 83% of American voters, would immediately enhance safety by ensuring vehicle owners can choose where and how their vehicles are professionally repaired.

Key points from Hanvey’s testimony included:

Cost and safety impacts on consumers : Manufacturer-imposed data restrictions are forcing vehicle owners into franchised dealerships, where repair costs are, on average, 36% higher and wait times significantly longer.

Real-world safety consequences : Independent repair shops are routinely unable to complete even basic repairs—such as battery replacements or windshield wiper changes—without dealer-only codes, resulting in unnecessary delays and added risk for drivers.

Economic and workforce implications : Independent repair shops perform more than 70% of out-of-warranty repairs nationwide and are critical to local economies, workforce development, and vehicle uptime for working families and commercial fleets.

Cybersecurity and intellectual property protections: The REPAIR Act preserves existing intellectual property rights and cybersecurity standards  manufacturers use to deliver data to franchised dealers.

Commercial vehicle safety: With only about 5,600 medium- and heavy-duty truck dealerships nationwide, independent and mobile repair providers are essential to keeping commercial fleets operating safely, especially in rural and remote regions.

Hanvey warned that without federal action, the automotive aftermarket faces an existential threat that would lead to a vertically integrated industry, reduced competition, higher prices, diminished quality, and fewer choices for consumers.

“The REPAIR Act is pro-consumer, pro-safety, and pro-competition,” Hanvey said. “It simply ensures that vehicle owners can access the repair and maintenance data necessary to keep their vehicles safe and on the road—just as they always have.”

Learn more about the REPAIR Act and send a letter to Congress today at repairact.com.

BETHESDA, Md. – Sept. 10, 2025 – Great Place To Work® and Fortune magazine selected the Auto Care Association for the 2025 Fortune Best Workplaces in Consulting and Professional Services™ List. Earning a spot at 35 on this list recognizes the Auto Care Association as one of the best companies to work for in the country. This is the fourth recognition the Auto Care Association has earned for great workplaces and comes in addition to earning the certification of “Great Place to Work” both in 2024 and again in 2025 as well as 2025 Best Small Workplace.

The Best Workplaces in Consulting and Professional Services award is based on an analysis of survey responses from nearly 149,000 employees at Great Place To Work Certified™ companies in the consulting and professional services industry.

“This recognition is a direct reflection of our incredible team,” said Bill Hanvey, president and CEO, Auto Care Association. “Their passion and commitment make this such a special place to work. We’re proud to celebrate them and thankful for everything they do to make honors like this possible.”

The Best Workplaces in Consulting and Professional Services list is highly competitive. Great Place To Work, the global authority on workplace culture, determines its lists using its proprietary Trust Index™ Survey to evaluate and certify thousands of organizations in America’s largest ongoing annual workforce study, based on more than 1.3 million survey responses and data from companies representing more than 8.4 million employees.

“We’re incredibly proud to once again be recognized as a Great Place to Work, now with the additional honor of being named among the best in consulting and professional services,” said Lea Diamond, senior vice president, people operations, Auto Care Association. “These achievements reflect the culture of trust, collaboration, respect—and most importantly, fun—that our employees build every day. Earning back-to-back certifications and this new recognition reinforces our commitment to creating an environment where people feel valued, supported, and inspired to grow.”

Survey responses reflect a comprehensive picture of the workplace experience. Honorees were selected based on their ability to offer positive outcomes for employees regardless of job role, race, gender, sexual orientation, work status or other demographic identifier.

To learn more about working at Auto Care Association, view the association’s Great Place To Work profile or visit https://www.autocare.org/about-us/working-at-auto-care .

9月11日， 银企行合作赋能汽摩配企业抱团出海暨共建上海国际汽配永久展馆战略发展大会 在上海国际汽车城瑞立酒店召开。本次大会是银、行、企三方协同的一次集中呈现—— 银行赋能给金融支持，行业商会做纽带，企业作为主体积极参与 。三方各尽其责、各展所长，上海国际汽配永久展馆的生态协同效应与平台优势进一步显现。展馆聚微成炬，让分散在产业基地乡镇里的中小汽摩配企业抱团出海，这束火炬，正成为指引中小企业走向全球市场的方向。

全国政协委员、全国工商联汽摩配商会常务会长杨英 在致辞中指出，当前中小企业单独出海成本高、渠道窄、风险大。永久展馆探索的 “基 地制造 、上海展贸、销往全球” 新模式，是商会服务全国会员企业的重要抓手。“永久展馆就是全国汽摩配行业抱团出海的事业起点。”她结合自身在印尼、越南建厂的经历坦言，单打独斗确实非常无奈，呼吁中小企业抱团出海。

上海市政协委员、上海新兴产业投资促进会执行会长、上海致盛实业集团董事长张润斌 表示，上海是我国对外开放的前沿窗口，嘉定更是中国汽车产业的高地。他坦言，中小制造业主体仍面临信息不对称、融资渠道窄、抗风险能力弱等难题，单靠企业单兵作战走不快、走不远。 上海新兴产业促进会将联动金融投资机构、产业园区和 各行业商 协会，主动参与永久展馆的资源对接与产业协同。

上海国际汽车城集团党委委员、副总经理陈杰 ，把汽 车城 25 年产业积 淀与永久展馆的落地逻辑讲得很透。 “无论是一个区域的发展，还是零部件企业发展，都离不开金融和资金的支持。 ” 如今汽车城已集聚上汽大众整车基地，以及理想、蔚来、舍弗勒等企业的研发中心。 他说， 永久展馆落在汽车城，看中的正是“客户就在身边”的产业生态——“好项目不缺空间，好项目不缺资源。 ”

全国工商联汽摩配商会会长、瑞立集团董事长张晓平 发表主旨演讲。 他给出硬核数据：据浙江省汽摩配行业商会统计，浙江全省中小汽摩配企业超过2.6万家，今年全省汽车及零部件产值有望突破1.4万亿元，大部分来自中小企业的配件出口和后市场。“浙江汽配产业的活力和潜力在哪里？在零部件，在中小企业，在出海。”

张晓平指出，中国整车出口今年有望突破 1000 万辆，未来中国汽配出口和海外配套市场将是超万亿级新蓝海。“ 不出海就出局。出海 是加法，不 是减法，企业的总部、税收、产能根基在国内。 ”他强调，中小汽摩配企业单打独斗的时代已经过去，“一个外商到温州、台州汽配制造基地，一天看 4 家企业，待十天也只能看 40 家。 在永久展馆，一天可以看一两千家企业。跑一家胜过跑百家千家。 ”

中国建设银行总行公司业务部资深副经理董宣忠 代表金融机构发声。他表示，建设银行推出“善建智造”“善建科技”两大专项方案，为汽摩配企业智能化改造、产能扩容、品牌出海提供全链条金融赋能。“ 金融正在加快转向服务实体经济。企业在抱团出海的同时，金融也在探讨如何走向全球，我们的目标是一致的。 ”

当天到场的银行阵容强大：建行总行及浙江、上海、广东、江苏、安徽、苏州等分行，农行温州分行、金华分行、丽水分行，民生银行温州分行，工行、邮储、浦发、温州银行瑞安支行等数十家金融机构负责人出席。一张覆盖跨境结算、贸易融资、风险规避的金融服务网络正在永久展馆周边织密。

银行给金融支持，商会做纽带、做服务，企业做主体、做产品——各出一块拼图，拼出的正是永久展馆这个“抱团出海”的产业生态。

永久展馆不仅是物理空间，更是链接全产业链的超级枢纽。当天，来自成都、青岛、山西、宿迁、廊坊、丽水、衢州、达州、南通、贵阳等全国各地的公交集团负责人近百人齐聚永久展馆，带着合作需求而来。通过“国企实力 + 民企活力，成就新质生产力”的协同发展模式， 新瑞立 已与全国 25 个省 110 家公交公司达成合作，公交系统的终端场景将与汽配供应链在永久展馆深度打通。

大会现场，永久展馆分别与河北再制造协会、 GL 出海联盟 达成战略合作，共同打造再制造汽车零部件展厅、GL出海联盟展厅。

从再制造零部件到出海联盟，从跨境电商到法律咨询、仲裁机构，永久展馆正在构建“保姆式”服务闭环，真正实现“进永久展馆，做全球生意”。

大会期间，滁州市委书记吴劲、副市长后其洁一行到访永久展馆参观交流，明确表示要加快推进滁州城市产业会客厅的打造，加快推进滁州公交公司与新瑞立的合作。这是永久展馆城市会客厅版图持续扩容的又一进展。

新瑞立 COO 徐本光发布年度发展报告：新瑞立在全国布局 265 家门店，拥有 30 多万个 SKU 和 1500 家战略供应商，合作客户超过 22 万，产品出口覆盖 100多 个国家和地区。

永久展馆组委会执行主任朱仲升介绍，展馆总建筑面积 5.3 万平方米，规划入驻 3000 家企业，目前入驻已超 2000 家，已建成 21 个城市会客厅。 12 月 1 日，永久展馆将正式全面开馆，届时全国汽摩配商会年会同期举行， 12 月 2 日 法兰克福展 在上海开幕，三大盛会能量叠加。 开馆前将冲刺 3000 家企业入驻，打造 100 个城市会客厅。

大会期间，巴西国际采购团一行 20 余人到访永久展馆，重点筛选中国质优价平的汽车零部件源头工厂，同时考察工程机械零部件供应链资源。 采购团对展馆“ 3000 余家源头制造企业、 365 天常态化运营”的模式高度认可。本次来访，搭建了中巴汽车后市场产业链合作桥梁，助力中国汽配企业开拓广阔的巴西市场。

组委会副主任、首席跨境电商专家李智荣拆解“一链一网一平台”数字化体系，为入驻企业实现全年 365 天、 24 小时不间断全球获客。新瑞立采购总监金丽敏发布国内国际双市场采购需求，将优先对接永久展馆已入驻企业。

答谢晚宴上，瑞安市惠华汽车机油泵有限公司董事长钱继续的一番话，道出了无数中小汽配企业主的心声。

“我们做机油泵的，产品藏在发动机最里面，车开了 20 万公里车主都看不到；我们的厂藏在小镇上，默默无闻。”钱继续动情地说，“我们这一行，一年要跑 50 多个展会，累得半死，但展会一结束，灯一关，人就散了。我们最缺的，不是手艺，是被看见。”

他把展馆广告贴在自己车上，跑遍杭州、宁波、广州。“ 以前是我去找客户，三天展会一散场，回去也没几个。现在是展馆让客户找得到我。 ”他说，一年 2 万元投入，换来的是 365 天的展示和全球流量对接，“这笔账，每一个务实的企业家都算得清楚。”

“相信才能看到，不是看到了才相信。”钱继续说，“我不是站在门口等客户，我是在屋里点一盏灯。今天这盏灯就是上海国际汽配永久展馆，灯已经点亮了， 365 天不灭。”

大会期间，钱继续又追加了一个展位。从“试试看”到“再加一个”，这位做机油泵的企业主，用最实在的方式投出了自己的信任票。

像钱继续这样的中小企业，正是中国汽配产业最真实的底色。浙江 2.6 万家中小汽摩配企业，九成藏在乡镇里，有手艺、有产品，却缺少被世界看见的窗口。让中小企业被看见——这是上海国际汽配永久展馆的初心。 当 2000 多家这样的企业聚在一起，微光便开始汇聚成星海。

但“被看见”只是第一步。 中国汽配品牌向上，正在经历从“被看见”到“被相信”的关键一跃。 永久展馆要做的，正是帮助中小企业在被看见的基础上，用 365 天不间断的展示、稳定的品质、银企护航的信用背书，一步步赢得全球采购商的信任。

截至本次大会，上海国际汽配永久展馆已吸引超过 2000 家企业入驻。 从 2000 家到 3000 家，从 21 个城市会客厅到 100 个，永久展馆的版图还在加速扩大。

银、行、企各尽其责，公交、保险、展会企业等生态伙伴协同共建，聚微成炬，众行致远。这束火炬，正照亮中国汽配产业从“单打独斗”走向“抱团共赢”、从“被看见”走向“被相信”的征途。

以及建行总行、浙江省分行、上海市分行、广东省分行、江苏省分行、安徽省分行、苏州分行，农行温州分行、金华分行、丽水分行，建行温州分行、嘉定支行、马鞍山分行、常州分行、泰州分行、嘉兴分行、湖州分行、台州分行、绍兴分行、丽水分行、舟山分行，农行瑞安支行，民生银行温州分行，工行瑞安支行，邮储瑞安支行，浦发瑞安支行，温州银行瑞安支行，中信银行嘉兴平湖支行、海盐支行，招商银行虹口支行等银行领导。

8月28日，政行企联动·走进上海永久展馆·赋能汽摩配企业内外贸一体化发展大会在上海国际汽车城瑞立酒店举行。本次大会由全国工商联汽摩配商会、上海国际汽车城集团、长三角汽车后市场产销合作产业链联盟联合主办，瑞立集团·新瑞立汽配连锁承办。

全国多地驻沪办、工信（经信）系统领导为主，工商联、商务、招商、开发区等政府有关单位负责人、各地商协会共同参会； 共商、共建上海国际汽配永久展馆100个城市会客厅。

从1月瑞安首站启航到8月入驻企业突破1700家，上海国际汽配永久展馆正加速成型。大会期间，永久展馆正式官宣： 银企战略合作千人大会定于9月11日在上海国际汽车城瑞立酒店举行。多位与会嘉宾表示，随着入驻企业持续增加，展馆核心铺位资源日趋紧张，9月11日千人大会后很可能出现一铺难求的局面。政行企三方正式从“走进”迈向“共建”。

上海市嘉定区人民政府副区长丁炯炯 在致辞中表示，上海国际汽配永久展馆作为赋能产业的重要载体， 已吸引1700家企业入驻。 展馆集常态展示、精准对接、专业招商、综合服务于一体，充分发挥嘉定汽车产业集聚和资源链接优势。 嘉定将持续优化营商环境，完善产业支持政策，为企业提供全周期、全方位的支持， 助力打通国内国际市场渠道，实现内外贸协同发展。

中国民营经济研究会常务理事、浙江省政府特约研究员、浙商研究中心副主任蔡晓春 在致辞中，一针见血地指出了大会主题的关键转变： “走进”是被动的参观、临时的使用；“共建”是主动的参与、长期的投入。

他指出，当前汽摩配产业面临整零协同不充分、出海体系化能力不足、跨界转型存在技术鸿沟三大痛点，解决这些问题需要“有为政府+有效市场+友好生态”三方协同。 共建永久展馆意味着三个转变：政府从管理者转变为赋能者，商协会从联谊会转变为资源整合平台，展馆从交易场转变为价值共创平台。新瑞立+永久展馆是双轮驱动，本质是产业互联网与实体展贸的深度融合。 只有三方联动，才能让中小企业“出海有保障、回来有港湾”。

湖北省人民政府驻上海办事处主任周彬 ，用湖北汽摩配企业抱团入驻永久展馆的实践，分享了驻沪办赋能地方产业内外贸一体化发展的经验。湖北正打造“ 武孝襄随十 ”万亿级汽车产业新格局， 依托永久展馆已落地十堰、襄阳两大会客厅，近百家鄂企入驻运营。 展馆对地方企业形成三重赋能：帮助立足上海、辐射全球，擦亮区域品牌；精准对接长三角主机厂与海内外贸易商；搭建商务洽谈平台助力内外贸融合发展。

全国工商联汽摩配商会会长、瑞立集团董事长张晓平 在主旨发言中指出，国内汽车市场已高度内卷，未来五到十年将迎来深度洗牌。而海外万亿级蓝海正加速打开，今年中国整车出口有望突破1000万台。 结论只有六个字：不出海，就出局。

针对部分地方政府担心企业“走出去”会导致产业空心化，张晓平算了一笔账： 出海不是减法而是加法，是“在国内做存量、在海外做增量”。 企业发展好了，总部、税收、产能的根还在当地。把企业搭载在永久展馆平 台上等于给企业 装上翅膀 ， 企业的市场越能海阔天空，企业的根就能扎得越稳，对当地“栽好梧桐树、养好金凤凰”就越有利。

上海国际汽车城集团党委委员、副总经理陈杰 介绍，作为全国汽车产业集聚度最高的区域之一，汽车城已汇聚上汽大众、蔚来、理想、博世等头部企业，每年举办200余场产业会议，持续凝聚行业核心力量。 依托高度集中的产业资源，永久展馆打造了一站式高效对接平台，外商单日即可触达上千家企业，效率远超传统考察模式。 放眼全球，汽车城正谋划公共出海平台，为企业拓展国际市场赋能，推动产业链抱团出海，形成全球化竞争合力。

上海国际汽配永久展馆组委会执行主任朱仲升 汇报最新数据： 展馆入驻企业已超1700家，11月底冲刺3000家。 总建筑面积 5.3万平 方米，已建成20个城市产业会客厅。传统展会三五天热闹，永久展馆365天细水长流， 200多批国内外商贸代表团，体现了蓬勃的产业能量。

上海国际汽配永久展馆组委会副主任、首席跨境电商专家李智荣 详解“一链一网一平台”线上线下闭环：3000家供应链为“一链”，全域流量网为“一网”，产业互联网平台为“一平台”， 七个维度流量来源实现全年不间断全球获客 。

新瑞立采购总监金丽敏 发布百亿采购计划： 去年采购超30亿元，未来5年将冲向每年百亿的采购额， 其 中出口50亿元，将优先对接入驻企业。 平台对外全面开放，入驻企业品牌将通过海外20多场专业展会持续曝光。

大会现场， 张晓平分别与国家外贸转型升级基地（上海嘉定·汽车及零部件）副总经理徐明、 星鼎荟中国汽车后市场企业家俱乐部 洪耿戈签署战略合作协 议。 这标志着永久展馆的“共建”朋友圈再扩容——嘉定基地带 来政策与口 岸资源，广东星鼎荟注入渠道与市场活力 ， 长三角和大湾区加强联动， 内外贸一体化发展再提速。

浙江省工商联原二级巡视员刘志义 用“五个五”为大会做总结： 五彩缤纷、五业并举、五富临门、五家兴旺、五站共进。

正如蔡晓春所说： “只要政府、行业、企业三方心往一处想，真正以共建者的姿态投身于永久展馆，就一定能在全球市场的星辰大海中开辟崭新未来。”

从“走进”到“共建”，这场政行企的双向奔赴正在改写 中国汽摩配 的出海叙事。大会现场同步官宣：银企战略合作千人大会定于9月11日在上海国际汽车城瑞立酒店举行。部分与会嘉宾表示，随着入驻企业持续增加，展馆核心铺位资源日趋紧张，9月11日千人大会后很可能出现一铺难求的局面。

浙江省工商联原副书记、副主席、一级巡视员，中国民营经济研究会常务理事、浙江省政府特约研究员、浙商研究中心副主任蔡晓春；

以及来自上海、天津、重庆、浙江、安徽、湖北、吉林、江西、河北、山西、四川等省级工信、驻沪办、贸促会部门有关单位领导，和广州、合肥、青岛、南京、长春、南昌、西安、太原、昆明、贵阳、包头、宁波、温州、湖州、绍兴、嘉兴、滁州、宣城、马鞍山、黄石、邯郸、开封、曲阜、綦江、永川、铜梁、扬州、宜春、九江、黄山、汉中、蚌埠、广元、淮北、济宁、南充、绵阳、丽水、烟台、伊犁州、枣庄、许昌、聊城、安庆、德阳、内江、宝鸡、盐城、诸暨、江都、乐清、瑞安、龙湾、瓯海、平阳、泗洪、桐城、余干、安吉、澄迈、大连金浦新区、清河、太仓、宁津、南浔、龙口等地方经信工信、驻沪办、工商联、商务、招商、开发区等省市县区相关单位领导。
